Methodology and limitations

  • Daily returns are calculated from the adjusted-price series provided in prices_wide.csv.
  • The portfolio is the arithmetic equal-weight average of the five stock daily returns.
  • Annualization uses 252 trading days. CAGR uses the number of daily observations divided by 252.
  • Sharpe ratio assumes a 0% annual risk-free rate for this baseline.
  • Historical 95% and 99% VaR are positive loss thresholds based on the 5th and 1st return percentiles.
  • Expected Shortfall is the average loss among observations at or below the corresponding return percentile.
  • Alpha is an annualized arithmetic-return estimate with a 0% risk-free rate, not a factor-model alpha.
  • The benchmark is the S&P 500 index series. The portfolio and index may have different investability and dividend conventions depending on the input data.
  • No taxes, transaction costs, slippage, financing costs, or execution constraints are included.
  • This is historical analytics, not the Monte Carlo simulation stage and not investment advice.

Research foundations

  • Markowitz (1952), Portfolio Selection — Journal of Finance.
  • Artzner et al. (1999), Coherent Measures of Risk — Mathematical Finance.
  • Acerbi & Tasche (2002), On the Coherence of Expected Shortfall — Journal of Banking & Finance.
  • Glasserman (2003), Monte Carlo Methods in Financial Engineering — Springer.
